message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Nightly Alt JDK Matrix Test

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '42 1 * * *' # Runs every day at 01:42 UTC on main branch only
  push:
    branches:
      - '*.x'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      jdk-versions:
        description: 'JDK versions to test (comma-separated, e.g., "17,21")'
        required: false
        default: '17,21'
        type: string
      modules:
        description: 'Maven modules to test (comma-separated paths, or "default" for predefined list)'
        required: false
        default: 'default'
        type: string
      baseline-jdk:
        description: 'Baseline JDK version for building'
        required: false
        default: '25'
        type: string
      skip-build:
        description: 'Skip the build step and only run tests'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: read

jobs:
  prepare-matrix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      jdk-matrix: ${{ steps.set-matrix.outputs.jdk-matrix }}
      modules: ${{ steps.set-matrix.outputs.modules }}
      baseline-jdk: ${{ steps.set-matrix.outputs.baseline-jdk }}
    steps:
      - name: Prepare matrix
        id: set-matrix
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Get input values or use defaults
          JDK_VERSIONS="${{ github.event.inputs.jdk-versions }}"
          JDK_VERSIONS="${JDK_VERSIONS:-17,21}"
          
          MODULES="${{ github.event.inputs.modules }}"
          MODULES="${MODULES:-default}"
          
          BASELINE_JDK="${{ github.event.inputs.baseline-jdk }}"
          BASELINE_JDK="${BASELINE_JDK:-25}"
          
          # Convert comma-separated JDK versions to JSON array
          IFS=',' read -ra JDK_ARRAY <<< "$JDK_VERSIONS"
          JDK_JSON="["
          for jdk in "${JDK_ARRAY[@]}"; do
            jdk_trimmed=$(echo "$jdk" | xargs)
            if [ -z "$JDK_JSON" ] || [ "$JDK_JSON" = "[" ]; then
              JDK_JSON="$JDK_JSON\"$jdk_trimmed\""
            else
              JDK_JSON="$JDK_JSON,\"$jdk_trimmed\""
            fi
          done
          JDK_JSON="$JDK_JSON]"
          
          # Use default modules if not specified
          if [ "$MODULES" = "default" ]; then
            MODULES="server/tests,"
            MODULES+="counter,"
            MODULES+="lock,"
            MODULES+="multimap,"
            MODULES+="cdi/embedded,"
            MODULES+="archetypes/embedded,"
            MODULES+="jcache/embedded,"
            MODULES+="jcache/tck-runner-embedded,"
            MODULES+="spring/embedded,"
            MODULES+="spring/spring6/spring6-embedded,"
            MODULES+="spring/spring7/spring7-embedded,"
            MODULES+="spring/spring-boot-3/embedded,"
            MODULES+="spring/spring-boot-3/it-tests/embedded-tests,"
            MODULES+="spring/spring-boot-4/embedded,"
            MODULES+="spring/spring-boot-4/it-tests/embedded-tests"
          fi
          
          {
            echo "jdk-matrix=$JDK_JSON"
            echo "modules=$MODULES"
            echo "baseline-jdk=$BASELINE_JDK"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  build-and-test-alternate-jdk:
    permissions:
      checks: write
    needs: prepare-matrix
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      MAVEN_OPTS: "-Xmx1500m -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError"
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        jdk: ${{ fromJson(needs.prepare-matrix.outputs.jdk-matrix) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v6

      - name: Cache Maven packages
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.m2/repository
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-maven-${{ hashFiles('**/pom.xml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-maven-

      - name: Setup Java (baseline JDK ${{ needs.prepare-matrix.outputs.baseline-jdk }})
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          java-version: ${{ needs.prepare-matrix.outputs.baseline-jdk }}
          distribution: 'zulu'

      - name: Build Infinispan with baseline JDK
        if: ${{ github.event.inputs.skip-build != 'true' }}
        run: ./mvnw -q clean install -Pdistribution -DskipTests -Dcheckstyle.skip

      - name: Setup alternate JDK ${{ matrix.jdk }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          java-version: ${{ matrix.jdk }}
          distribution: 'zulu'

      - name: Run tests with alternate JDK ${{ matrix.jdk }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Set JAVA_ALT_HOME to the alternate JDK path
          export JAVA_ALT_HOME=$JAVA_HOME
          ./mvnw -q verify \
            -pl ${{ needs.prepare-matrix.outputs.modules }} \
            -Pjava-alt-test \
            -Denforcer.skip=true \
            -Dmaven.test.failure.ignore=true \
            -Dansi.strip=true \
            -B -e

      - name: Upload surefire test report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7
        with:
          name: surefire-test-report-JDK${{ matrix.jdk }}
          path: |
            **/target/*-reports*/**/TEST-*.xml
            !**/target/*-reports*/**/TEST-*FLAKY.xml
            !**/ignored*reports*
            **/*.dump*
            **/hs_err_*
            **/*.hprof

      - name: Upload log files
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7
        with:
          name: log-files-JDK${{ matrix.jdk }}
          compression-level: 9
          path: |
            **/*.log
            !**/*[:"<>\*\?]*/**/*.log
            !**/*[:"<>\*\?]*.log
      - name: Publish Test Report
        if: always()
        uses: ctrf-io/github-test-reporter@dbb08957b5b2af918b39136ab2c5532002c7649b # v1
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        with:
          report-path: '**/*-reports*/**/TEST-*.xml'
          failed-folded-report: 'true'
          write-ctrf-to-file: './ctrf-reports/ctrf-report.json'
          exit-on-fail: 'true'
          status-check: 'true'
          status-check-name: 'Nightly Alt JDK ${{ matrix.jdk }} Test'
          integrations-config: |
            {
              "junit-to-ctrf": {
                "enabled": true,
                "action": "convert",
                "options": {
                  "output": "./ctrf-reports/ctrf-report.json",
                  "toolname": "junit-to-ctrf",
                  "useSuiteName": false,
                  "env": {
                    "appName": "my-app"
                  }
                }
              }
            }",
  "rationale": "Add Maven dependency caching (actions/cache@v4) for ~/.m2/repository with a key based on hashFiles('**/pom.xml') to avoid repeated dependency downloads on each workflow run. The experiment evidence (experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-a89d5fd8d30bc8cb-r2) demonstrates a 51% elapsed time reduction (145s → 71s median) for a similar Maven-based Java matrix workflow. This optimization preserves all build and test coverage, requires no behavior changes, and is safe for scheduled, push, and manual triggers. The workflow currently has no caching step, and the repository uses Maven with multiple pom.xml files across modules, making dependency caching highly applicable.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-a89d5fd8d30bc8cb-r2"]
}

Let me analyze this workflow and the evidence to determine what optimization to apply.

The workflow is a nightly JDK matrix test for Infinispan. It:
1. Runs on schedule (daily at 01:42 UTC), on push to *.x branches, and on workflow_dispatch
2. Has a prepare-matrix job that sets up the JDK matrix and modules to test
3. Has a build-and-test-alternate-jdk job that:
   - Builds with a baseline JDK (default 25)
   - Then tests with alternate JDKs (default 17, 21)
   - Uses Maven with various profiles and options

Looking at the evidence provided:

1. **P-LIT-GHA-CACHE** (Cache dependency downloads) - This pattern shows caching Maven packages (~/.m2/repository) with a key based on pom.xml hash. The experiment example shows a 51% elapsed time savings.

2. **P-LIT-FAIL-FAST** (Cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure) - The workflow currently has `fail-fast: false` in the matrix strategy. The evidence shows this can save resources when a matrix failure makes remaining results dispensable.

3. **P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT** (Bound jobs with a custom timeout) - The workflow doesn't have any timeout set. The evidence shows this can reduce runaway consumption.

4. **P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE** (Cancel superseded runs) - This is a scheduled workflow, so superseded runs could be relevant.

5. **P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE** (Pause repeatedly failing scheduled workflows) - The CI history shows 5 consecutive failures on schedule runs. This pattern could apply.

Let me check the workflow more carefully:

The workflow has:
- `strategy.fail-fast: false` in the matrix job
- No timeout on the job
- No Maven dependency caching
- Scheduled runs that have been failing consecutively

The most applicable optimizations based on the evidence:

1. **Maven caching (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE)** - The experiment example shows adding a cache step for ~/.m2/repository with key based on pom.xml hash. This is directly applicable since this is a Maven project.

2. **Fail-fast (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST)** - The workflow explicitly sets `fail-fast: false`. The evidence shows changing to `fail-fast: true` can save resources when matrix failures make remaining jobs dispensable. However, the contraindication says "Every matrix outcome is required" - we need to check if all JDK test results are required.

3. **Custom timeout (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT)** - No timeout is set, could add one.

4. **Fail-schedule (P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE)** - 5 consecutive failures on schedule, but this requires a monitored pause/resume policy.

Looking at the experiment evidence for P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-a89d5fd8d30bc8cb-r2), it shows a 51% elapsed time savings by adding Maven cache. This is a measured CI workflow on fork with actual metrics.

The workflow builds with Maven and downloads dependencies each time. Adding a cache for ~/.m2/repository would be beneficial.

Also, the workflow has `fail-fast: false` explicitly set. The P-LIT-FAIL-FAST pattern shows changing this to `true` can save resources. However, the contraindication is "Every matrix outcome is required". In this case, the workflow tests multiple JDK versions (17, 21) and uploads test reports for each. If one JDK fails, do we still need results from the others? The workflow uploads artifacts and publishes test reports for each JDK separately, and uses `maven.test.failure.ignore=true`. This suggests they want to collect results from all JDKs even if some fail. So fail-fast might not be appropriate.

The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern shows adding a timeout to the job. The workflow doesn't have one, and the evidence shows 26.8% savings in one experiment.

The P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE pattern requires "A monitored pause/resume policy is approved" which we don't know if exists.

Given the evidence, the most strongly supported optimization with measured benefits is **Maven dependency caching (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE)** with the experiment showing 51% elapsed time savings. The workflow uses Maven and downloads dependencies every run.

Let me also check if there's already a cache - looking at the workflow, there's no cache step currently.

The experiment example for P-LIT-GHA-CACHE shows exactly this pattern: adding a cache step for ~/.m2/repository with key based on hashFiles('**/pom.xml').

I'll propose adding the Maven cache step. This is a minimal, safe change that preserves all build and test coverage.

Let me also consider if we should add a timeout. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT experiment shows 26.8% savings, but it's for a different type of workflow (Node.js). The Maven build might take longer. Without knowing the typical runtime, it's harder to set an appropriate timeout.

The fail-fast change has contraindications that might apply here since they seem to want all JDK results.

So I'll go with adding the Maven cache (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE) as the primary optimization, supported by the experiment evidence.

Wait, let me check the evidence IDs more carefully. The experiment for P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is documented in two chunks (chunk_index 0 and 1) but they're from the same document_id: "experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-a89d5fd8d30bc8cb-r2". The pattern_id is "P-LIT-CONFIG-REUSE" in the experiment but the pattern catalogue shows "P-LIT-GHA-CACHE" as the pattern for caching dependency downloads.

Actually, looking at the experiment evidence, the pattern_id is "P-LIT-CONFIG-REUSE" but the content shows adding a Maven cache. The pattern catalogue has "P-LIT-GHA-CACHE" for "Cache dependency downloads". The experiment seems to be demonstrating the cache pattern but labeled as CONFIG-REUSE. Let me use the pattern catalogue ID "P-LIT-GHA-CACHE" since that's the canonical pattern for this optimization.

The experiment document_id is "experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-a89d5fd8d30bc8cb-r2" and it shows the cache addition with 51% savings.

I'll propose adding the Maven cache step to the build-and-test-alternate-jdk job, after the checkout and before the build steps.

Let me construct the updated workflow.
